findings.summary: The four MAST-U panels render to byte-identical PNGs (md5 f7d3f1f632040a8c879dd3bcd8a8f47d for all four of the review-run attachments image-3.png through image-6.png, with identical pixel census: 7645 blue, 17429 grey, 96.3 percent white). Published as four figures, the set shows a reader one picture four times: the stored-default, stored-continuation, displaced-default and displaced-continuation arms cannot be told apart in the rendering, so the displaced arm the section exists to show contributes no distinct visual evidence. Whether this is one shared terminal state across the four arms or one picture assigned to all four cannot be decided from the raster, but either way the figure set carries no comparison a reader can act on.

The subject of these panels - the nova terminal iterate, the series the review exists to see - is drawn at linewidth=1.0 while the stored imas-efit reference above it is drawn at 2.6 pt (line 93), so the reference carries about three times the ink: measured 20462 grey against 6863 blue pixels on the ITER render and 21752 against 8280 on the TCV render. The project's own plot-style rule separates a comparison series by colour or dash, never by thinning it; here the blue contour also renders as the fainter of the two at page width, where the panel shrinks far below its 1400 px preview.

Every panel is drawn on a fixed 14x7.2 in canvas with a device-sized poloidal cross-section inside it, so the machine occupies 20 percent of the canvas width on ITER (content box x 560-841 of 1399 px) and 14-15 percent on the others, and 95.4-96.3 percent of all pixels are pure white. Roughly four fifths of each canvas is empty margin while the drawing that carries all the information is confined to a narrow column; on the page the contours and the legend become small relative to the surrounding prose, and a reader who wants the contour topology has the least legible object on the page.

The vessel is not clipped identically for the two series. The blue terminal-iterate contours are masked by whole triangulation cells, so along the ITER inner-wall edge a few blue strokes run a few pixels outside the drawn wall polyline, and a stray grey contour fragment sits between the wall and the blue there. On a panel whose whole purpose is to show where the solved field sits relative to the vessel, marks outside the vessel read as data the solve could not have produced.

The grey stored-state contours are bounded by the source grid rather than by the plasma, so they stop with blunt flat caps in open plasma - clearest across the MAST-U divertor notch and at the top of the TCV panel, where several grey strokes end mid-field, their outlines cut square. A reader cannot tell whether the field ends there or the plotting domain was cut, so those contour ends read as truncation rather than as data. Blue contours stop at the same vertical cut where the node mesh ends.
